Where it began

David Warner was born in Paddington, in Sydney's east, on 27 October 1986, and grew up in Matraville. At 13 a coach tried to turn him into a right-hander, because too many of his shots were going in the air. He went back to batting left-handed and promptly broke the under-16 run record at Sydney Coastal.

He played first grade for Eastern Suburbs at 15. In January 2009 he played a Twenty20 match for Australia before he had played a first-class game. No one had done that since 1877. He made 89 from 43 balls.

The player

His Test career began against New Zealand at Brisbane in December 2011, and he hit the winning runs. Less than two weeks later he carried his bat for 123 at Hobart, and in his fifth Test he reached a hundred against India at Perth in 69 balls on the way to 180.

In 112 Tests from 2011 to 2024 he made 8,786 runs at 44.60, with 26 hundreds and 37 fifties, and by November 2026 he ranked 23rd of all Test cricketers for both runs and hundreds. His best was 335 not out against Pakistan at Adelaide in 2019, the first triple hundred made at that ground. In 2017 at Sydney he became the first man to reach a Test hundred before lunch on day one in Australia. He made a double hundred in his 100th Test, in 2022, and signed off at the SCG in January 2024 with 57 in his last innings as Australia completed a clean sweep of Pakistan.

What made him special

He was not tall, at 170 cm, but strong forearms and a low centre of gravity let him hit the ball very hard and very high. He scored quickly in every format and could switch-hit when the mood took him.

His leg-spin was more of a hobby. His first ball in Tests brought a chance that went down in the outfield, and his four Test wickets cost 67.25 runs apiece, so it was probably wise that opening the batting stayed the day job.

Away from the middle

He won the Allan Border Medal three times, was named in the ICC's Test team of the decade for 2011 to 2020, and was in the Australian sides that took the World Cup in 2015 and 2023. He was also player of the tournament when Australia won the 2021 T20 World Cup. In the Indian Premier League he captained Sunrisers Hyderabad to the title in 2016.

In 2015 he married Candice Falzon, the former Ironwoman, so the family was not short of athletes.

And finally

In February 2024 he became the first Australian to play 100 matches for his country in each format, and he was player of the match in the 100th game of all three. For a man once thought too keen on hitting the ball in the air, it worked out rather well.
